sentences.text: This appeal filed by the appellants/claimants under Section 173(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 arises out of the award dated 21/08/2012 passed by the Additional Motor Accident Claims Tribunal (Fast Track Court), Sabalgarh District Morena (M.P.) (hereinafter referred to as the "Claims Tribunal") in Claim Case No.06/2012, on the ground of inadequacy of compensation, seeking enhancement thereof, and also on the ground that the Claims Tribunal, by passing the impugned award, has totally exonerated the Insurance Company from its liability to pay compensation.

entities.text: Additional Motor Accident Claims Tribunal (Fast Track Court), Sabalgarh District Morena
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 2. The date of the accident and the issue of negligence are not in dispute, and the findings recorded by the Claims Tribunal in this regard are not under challenge.
However, the dispute pertains to the liability.

3. As per the findings of the Claims Tribunal, in the case of death of Shivcharan Rawat in a motor accident, a total compensation of Rs.2,01,500/- has been awarded along with interest from the date of filing of the claim petition till its realization.
4. Learned counsel for the appellants submits that Claims Tribunal has committed a error awarding compensation in lower side.

It is also argued that the Insurance NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2026:MPHC-GWL:4788 2 MA-1250-2012 Company cannot be absolved of its liability to pay compensation to a third party and, even in case of breach of policy conditions, is required to first satisfy the award with liberty to recover the amount from respondents No.1 and 2.

entities.text: Smt. Baijanti Bai vs Rajesh Kumar B.L.
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is further contended that the total compensation of Rs.2,01,500/- awarded by the Claims Tribunal is grossly inadequate, necessitating the present appeal, and the appellants seek enhancement of Rs.2,00,000/- in addition to the awarded amount.
Hence, prayed for setting aside the impugned award.
5. On the other hand, learned counsel for the Insurance Company contended that the amount awarded by the Claims Tribunal is just and proper and needs no enhancement.
He supported the findings recorded by the Claims Tribunal and prays for dismissal of the appeal.

6. Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record of the Claims Tribunal.
7.
On perusal of the record, it is undisputed that deceased was a third party.
It is also undisputed that at the time of the alleged accident, owner and driver have no valid and effective permit.
So it is a complete breach of terms and conditions of the Insurance Policy.

8. In view of the judgments of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Amrit Paul Singh vs. TATA AIG General Insurance Co. Ltd. , 2019 (2) MPLJ (SC) 8, and National Insurance Co. Ltd. vs. Challa Bharathamma and others, 2004 ACJ 2094, even if the offending vehicle is operated without a valid and effective permit, the insurance company is liable to pay the compensation to the claimant in the first instance and thereafter recover the same from the owner and driver of the offending vehicle.

entities.text: Amrit Paul Singh vs. TATA AIG General Insurance Co. Ltd. , 2019 (2) MPLJ (SC) 8
entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.text: National Insurance Co. Ltd. vs. Challa Bharathamma and others, 2004 ACJ 2094
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 9. Accordingly, the finding recorded by the Claims Tribunal in this regard is modified to the extent that the Insurance Company shall pay the compensation amount to the claimants NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-GWL:4788 3 MA-1250-2012 with liberty to recover the same from the owner and driver of the offending vehicle.

10. So far as the contention of appellants with regard to enhancement of compensation is concerned,
this Court finds it appropriate to assess the income of the deceased as an unskilled person in view of the law laid down in the cases of Sukhdevi v. Devendra Kumar, ILR 2014 MP 172; Kanwar Devi v.
Bansal Roadways , 2008 ACJ 2182; and National Insurance Co. Ltd. v. Renu Devi, (2008) 3 ACC 134 in which it is held that when documentary proof of income is lacking, income is to be assessed as per the minimum wages applicable.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Therefore, in considered opinion of this Court, the just and proper amount of the income of the deceased as per Minimum Wages Act in the present case is Rs.3195/-
per month of an unskilled person.

11. As regard to loss of income including future prospects, in the light of judgment of National Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs. Pranay Sethi, 2017 ACJ 2700 , the claimants are entitled for loss of income including future prospects.

entities.text: National Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs. Pranay Sethi, 2017 ACJ 2700
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: As per Pranay Sethi (supra), future prospects @ 10% be assessed.

Further, as per the judgment of the Apex Court in the case of Sarla Verma and ors. Vs Delhi Transport Corporation and Anr. reported in (2009) 6 SCC 121 , even if age of the deceased is to be taken into account, multiplier of 11 should be applied.

entities.text: Sarla Verma and ors. Vs Delhi Transport Corporation and Anr. reported in (2009) 6 SCC 121
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Also, in view of the judgment passed by Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of United India Insurance Company Ltd. vs. Satinder Kaur and Others reported in 2020 ACJ 2131, the claimants are entitled to get compensation towards loss of Smt. 2 consortium and loss of estate.
12.

sentences.text:
Accordingly, the appellants/claimants are entitled to receive compensation under the following heads:-
 HEAD   Income Rs. 3195 x 1  After adding Future Prospects@10% Rs.3,834/-
 After deducting personal expenses 1/3 Rs.28,116/-
 Multiplier 11 Rs. 3,09,276  Other Heads:-
 Loss of Consortium Rs.40,000 X   NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-GWL:4788  4   Loss of Estate and funeral expenses Rs.30,000/
 Total = Rs.4,1 13.
Thus, the just and proper amount of compensation payable in the present case comes to Rs.4,19,276/- as against the sum of Rs.2,01,500/- awarded by the learned Claims Tribunal.
Accordingly, the appellants/claimants are held entitled to an additional compensation of Rs.2,17,776/- over and above the amount already awarded by the Tribunal.
14. Consequently, this miscellaneous appeal is partly allowed, and the compensation amount is enhanced by Rs.2,17,776/-.
The enhanced compensation shall carry interest at the same rate as awarded by the learned Claims Tribunal from the date of filing of claim petition till its realization.
The enhanced amount shall be paid to the appellants within a period of three months from the date of receipt of the certified copy of this order.
The remaining conditions imposed by the learned Claims Tribunal shall remain intact.

15. In case the enhanced compensation exceeds the valuation of the appeal, the appellants shall deposit the differential Court fee (if not already paid) within a period of one month from today and furnish proof of such payment before the Registry.
Upon compliance, the Registry shall issue the certified copy of this order.
16. In view of the foregoing discussion, the miscellaneous appeal stands disposed of accordingly.
